Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy , the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday (Nov 11), citing people familiar with the matter. The board is preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine his future, the report added. Earlier in the day, the New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The reports come days after Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife , as Nvidia's board investigates whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Nvidia's shares were down about 8 per cent in after-hours trading.

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 12 : Australia's blue-chip companies are increasingly invoking artificial intelligence as they cut jobs and move work offshore, unions and experts say, complicating the government's efforts to support employment in a slowing economy. On Tuesday, Qantas, Australia's flag carrier, said it would cut 850 jobs and outsource some corporate functions offshore as part of an AI-driven overhaul with consulting firm Accenture, a move that has raised accusations of "AI washing." "AI washing" describes a practice by companies of attributing layoffs to AI tools when the primary driver may be broader cost-cutting measures, such as shifting jobs offshore. Tech companies WiseTech and Atlassian have cut jobs this year, attributing the losses to AI. Telecommunications firm Telstra has also cut jobs from an AI joint venture with Accenture, with some work offshored to India.

More broadly, other firms across corporate Australia have also slashed their domestic headcounts while expanding operations in India, the Philippines and Vietnam, though they did not explicitly mention AI in their announcements. When asked about the Qantas job cuts, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who was unveiling the response to a recent breach of a government website by an OpenAI agent, said AI "represents an enormous opportunity and a major economic issue." Labour unions have argued that Australian workers were not being replaced by AI, but by lower-paid offshore employees. "Unions are concerned about the risk of companies using AI simply as a cover to cut Australian jobs with no accountability," said Australian Council of Trade Unions Secretary Melissa Donnelly. "From Qantas to the big banks, workers deserve transparency and genuine consultation over decisions that impact their jobs and lives." The Australian Services Union, which represents the affected Qantas workers, accused the airline of "using AI to launder their cuts to Australian jobs." "We expect to see more of this cost cutting and race to the bottom if corporate Australia continues to copy this failed tactic," said Assistant National Secretary Scott Cowen. Senator Barbara Pocock, a member of the Australian Greens party, said on Wednesday that she was concerned to see big companies engaging in "AI washing," using the technology as an excuse to cut jobs. "AI is transforming our workplaces and economy but that's no excuse to let it run rampant," Pocock said in a statement. A Qantas spokesperson said in a statement it would continue to consult with unions and that it was focused on "redeployment opportunities" and support for impacted staff. Qantas did not respond to the concerns around 'AI washing'. Atlassian, WiseTech and Telstra did not immediately respond to requests for comment. TREND TO CONTINUE Further job cuts by companies could pose headaches for Australia's centre-left Labor government, with recent polls showing its approval ratings steadily falling amid high cost-of-living pressures. The central bank has raised interest rates five times so far this year to their highest level in 18 years amid persistent inflation, while the latest data showed the unemployment rate at a five-year high of 4.7 per cent. Uri Gal, a professor at the University of Sydney Business School, said a growing number of companies were blaming job cuts on AI, but "we should therefore be cautious about accepting AI as the primary explanation." "There are real incentives to engage in AI washing," he said. "A company that announces job cuts to reduce costs may face criticism, whereas one that presents the same decision as part of an AI transformation can appear innovative and forward-looking." Gal said the Qantas decision appeared to be due to conventional outsourcing and demonstrated how AI can help justify restructuring before the technology's productivity gains have materialised. "The company has announced that some corporate functions will be transferred to Accenture, primarily in India, and explicitly states that these functions will subsequently be transformed through AI and automation," Gal said. "This raises an obvious question: if AI is making these jobs redundant, why does the work first need to be transferred to another group of employees?" The Reserve Bank of Australia said this week AI had not yet led to widespread job losses, though it noted "tentative signs of adjustment," with job ads weakening in AI-exposed occupations and employment growing more strongly in less affected roles. A government spokesperson said in a statement it expected Australian workers to see the benefits of new technologies and that employers should invest in upskilling them to adopt AI.

Source: Reuters

FAST

PARIS, Nov 11 : France's Alexia Barrier became the first woman to complete the Route du Rhum in the Ultim class on Wednesday, finishing fifth after a punishing transatlantic race that forced three of the eight giant trimarans to retire. The 46-year-old crossed the finish line in Pointe-a-Pitre at 1542 local time on Wednesday (1942 GMT) aboard IDEC Sport-CIC, completing the 3,542-nautical-mile race from Saint-Malo to Guadeloupe in 10 days, 7 hours and 40 minutes. She arrived more than three days behind her compatriot Tom Laperche, who skippered SVR-Lazartigue to victory in the Ultim class in record time. Thomas Coville, aboard Sodebo Ultim 3, was second and Louis Burton, skipper of Armand Thiery, took third, with LIAMM skipper Guirec Soudee finishing just off the podium.

Barrier struggled to match the leaders aboard IDEC Sport-CIC, the oldest Ultim in the fleet, launched in 2006. Ultim trimarans can measure up to 32 metres long and 23 metres wide (105 feet by 75 feet). But the strength and reliability of her boat enabled Barrier to finish the quadrennial race when three of her rivals failed to make it across the Atlantic. Armel Le Cleac'h, skipper of Maxi Banque Populaire XI, capsized off the Azores last Wednesday, three days after the start. The 2016-17 Vendee Globe winner was later rescued by a Panamanian cargo ship. Defending champion Charles Caudrelier retired from the race after suffering foil damage to his new Maxi Edmond de Rothschild-Gitana 18, while Actual Ultim 4 skipper Anthony Marchand withdrew because of a major problem with his central rudder. Barrier also endured problems of her own, attempting to repair a torn mainsail before encountering a winch issue in the closing days of the race. One of only 13 women to complete the Vendee Globe, Barrier also led the first all-female crew to complete the Jules Verne Trophy course 10 months ago and has again broken new ground in a discipline long dominated by men. Her next target is the Arkea Ultim Challenge, a solo race around the world for giant Ultim class trimarans, whose second edition is due to start in January 2028.

Source: Reuters

Nov 11 : Kylian Mbappe will not feature in France's Nations League match against Italy on Thursday as he is not fully fit, coach Zinedine Zidane told reporters on Wednesday. Mbappe missed France's last three matches after injuring his left knee while scoring the winner in their Nations League clash with Turkey on September 25. L'Equipe reported that Mbappe was troubled by a hamstring problem and had missed Wednesday's training session with the national team. "He will be out tomorrow. He felt a slight pain and, as usual, we won’t take any risks. Losing players is regrettable, but it’s part of the game. I hope it’s nothing serious and that we’ll have him back on Sunday," Zidane was quoted as saying by L'Equipe.

Nov 11 : The return of Jeremy Doku to the Belgium squad has handed coach Mark van Bommel a luxury problem, he said on Wednesday. Doku, who was ill during the World Cup and had a subdued tournament, missed the opening four matches of the new Nations League campaign in September and October because of injury. The winger is now fit, however, for their last two Group A1 fixtures against Turkey in Izmir on Thursday and Italy in Brussels on Sunday. "I'm very pleased to have Jeremy back in the squad," Van Bommel told a press conference.

He was already feeling it yesterday. He is still able to train, but we have mutually decided not to include him in the line-up," added the coach. Nov 11 : Australia centre Len Ikitau said the Wallabies must change their mindset for Sunday's test against Scotland at Murrayfield or risk another damaging defeat after last weekend’s record loss to England. The 2027 World Cup hosts went down 45-22 at Twickenham on Sunday, the most points Australia have conceded in a test against England. They face a Scotland side also seeking a response after losing heavily to New Zealand. "England kind of gave it to us from the start and put us on a load of pressure and played the way that they wanted to play and we kind of sat back and watched them," Ikitau said. "We can't be doing that against Scotland; we really want to be going out there, especially in defence, and put them under the pressure.

Ikitau said he had no idea why Australia were so flat at Twickenham.  "We had a great week ahead of the game, I thought the preparations were on point but sometimes you get to a game and you're just not there and I felt like we were off as a team and as a collective." One problem is finding a settled partnership in midfield. "We’re all over the shop at the moment and there have been some major fixes for us as a backline, working at training," Ikitau said. "It’s been pretty tough trying to stick with the same centre pairing, and being able to play consistently with the same people, but I feel like we've got a lot of good centres."

LONDON, Nov 11 : Harry Kane has spent much of the last decade rewriting the record books and on Thursday the striker will add another chapter when he becomes England's most-capped men's player with his 126th appearance against Croatia. Before kickoff at Wembley, the 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward will present the Ballon d'Or trophy he won last month to England's fans before moving past former goalkeeper Peter Shilton's long-standing record. "Definitely up there with the biggest (achievements of my career)," England captain Kane told reporters at former club Tottenham Hotspur's training ground on Wednesday after being given a standing ovation when he entered the room.

"It showcases consistency at the highest level and to reach the number of caps I have is a testament to the things I spoke about in my (Ballon d'Or) speech behind the scenes, the dedication and for sure it is one of the biggest milestones of my career." Kane is never one to shout his name from the rooftops, but having moved past Wayne Rooney's England scoring record of 53 goals in 2023 he has surged to 91 and ranks among his country's all-time greats, even if ending England's long wait for a major trophy has remained elusive. England manager Thomas Tuchel said Kane was the "perfect captain and a leader by example" and described his playing style as unique, adding that he is getting smarter with age. Asked if Kane is England's greatest player, Tuchel said: "I don't know but he is up there of course. It's now proven and it's always nice if things are proven. "He has his collection of prizes, he will score more goals, he will get more games and tomorrow he will start as captain of course. It's a big occasion to present the Ballon d'Or to our fans and bring it to the country and when he gets his all-time record for 126 matches. "It's a beautiful, beautiful occasion." PRESENTATION AT WEMBLEY Kane will be honoured in a pre-match presentation at Wembley before the UEFA Nations League match against Croatia with Shilton, who has held the England appearance record since 1989, also involved. Only a handful of active men's internationals have made more appearances for their countries than Kane, whose England debut came as a substitute against Lithuania in 2015 when he scored little more than a minute after coming on. Once the anthems have been sung and the record secured, Kane's attention will turn to the next target in a career that continues to gather milestones. "We spoke in the last camp about the 100 goals for England, I think that's another incredible milestone to try and reach as soon as possible," said Kane, who scored a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for Bayern Munich and England last season. "Right now, I'm feeling really, really good so hopefully many more years to see what else I can achieve. "To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream. I know how difficult that is so extremely motivated to do that."

LISBON: Airlines cancelled more than 200 flights in and out of Portugal , while schools and hundreds of supermarkets and businesses closed on Wednesday (Nov 11) as Storm Charles made landfall, bringing heavy downpours and gale-force winds. Although the storm was less severe than initially expected, the government, criticised for its slow response to a succession of storm s in January and February, had taken pre-emptive steps, putting all emergency services and army units on alert, cancelling classes, shutting non-essential public services and advising people to stay indoors. Portugal 's weather service IPMA said the eye of the storm had split in two over the Atlantic, diminishing its strength when it arrived via the southern Algarve region. It was expected to reach most of southern Portugal and the Lisbon region through late afternoon. Civil Protection Commander Mario Silvestre said authorities were maintaining high alert levels for flash floods, wind and rough seas after registering 538 incidents since midnight.

Storm Charles had already swept through the Madeira archipelago, causing some flooding and felling trees. Emergency services rescued a man swept away when water flooded his garage on the island of Madeira, but no casualties were reported. Since Sunday, Portugal and neighbouring Spain have been pummelled by heavy rains brought by Storm Bruna, with flooding reported in several areas including road tunnels in Lisbon, which were mostly shut on Wednesday. The new storm was expected to reach southwestern Spain on Wednesday afternoon, with the country's weather service AEMET warning of "serious or very serious" impact from heavy rain, strong winds and rough seas that could exacerbate conditions caused by Storm Bruna. In central Spain, authorities maintained the evacuation of more than 3,000 people in Piedralaves, whom they removed from their homes on Tuesday due to the risk of a local dam overflowing, and warned that rainfall was expected to intensify from midday.
